correctness.rationale: For smooth lattice polygon P, smooth toric jet-bundle/discriminant formula gives dual degree c(P)=3A-2B+V for hypersurface dual, primal degree A (A normalized area), and Pick+adjunction gives A=2g+B-2. Subtract yields 4g+V-4. Every smooth lattice triangle is unimodularly equivalent to d Delta: at its two other vertices primitive-edge determinants force a=b=gcd(a,b) after normalizing the first vertex. Interior count is (d-1)(d-2)/2 and d>=2 ensures nondefect, hence exactly triangular g permit excess 4g-1 uniquely. All other g have V>=4; rectangle [0,2]x[0,g+1] has genus g, four vertices, is smooth and for g>=1 nondefective, attaining 4g. Genus 0 nondefective quadratic Veronese d=2 attains -1; unimodular d=1 defective is explicitly excluded. Independent exact tests covered d2..39 and g0..99; they support but are not the proof.

originality.rationale: The standard smooth toric discriminant face-volume formula, Pick and adjunction are prior, while the fixed sectional-genus lower-envelope problem and sharp triangular-genus equality classification constitute a distinct explicit extremal theorem. Relevant full DNV paper provides c(P) but does not state this min_g result. This is an elementary but nontrivial synthesis of smooth triangle rigidity, existence at all remaining genera and discriminant identities.
residual_risks: A classical source may already state the elementary fixed-genus corollary in different terminology; unindexed genus-envelope observations remain possible.
Smooth/nondefective/complete embedding assumptions are indispensable; singular toric surfaces and noncomplete embeddings not claimed.

value.rationale: At fixed sectional genus, sharp excess of dual versus primal degree is a natural projective-geometric extremal invariant. The result classifies its all-genus envelope and unique three-vertex equality cases, with explicit four-vertex realizations elsewhere; the one-unit dips distinguish Veronese genera. The exact boundary is motivated by smooth lattice polygon geometry, not an arbitrary finite search.

limitations: Literature could contain a classic fixed-g corollary under alternate terminology; primary discriminant formula itself not novel.
